pr_title: agnhost image: use actual DNS domain instead of hardcoded cluster.local
pr_body:
'agnhost' image uses hardcoded 'cluster.local' value for DNS domain.
It leads to failure of a bunch of HPA tests when test cluster is
configured to use custom DNS domain and there is no alias for
default 'cluster.local' one.
So, fix it by reusing it's own function for reading DNS domain suffixes.

Bumps 'agnhost' image version to 2.24

Signed-off-by: Valerii Ponomarov <kiparis.kh@gmail.com>

issue_context.title: Resource consumer controller does not respect configured dns domain
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
During execution of HPA e2e part on kubespray deployment environment with non-default domain 7 of 8 HPA tests failed. One passed by accident due it require only downscale.

**What you expected to happen**:
All 8 tests passed

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Deploy a Kubernetes cluster using any desired tool with any domain setting that differs from cluster.local
2. Execute e2e tests with regex [Feature:HPA]

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Discovered using metrics server 0.3.6.
Domain set to different than default

During normal execution was observed that creating of consume requests doing nothing.
```
Mar  3 01:27:04.782: INFO: RC test-deployment: sending request to consume 325 millicores
Mar  3 01:27:04.782: INFO: ConsumeCPU URL: {https   172.19.116.45:443 /api/v1/namespaces/horizontal-pod-autoscaling-470/services/test-deployment-ctrl/proxy/ConsumeCPU  false durationSec=30&millicores=325&requestSizeMillicores=100 }
Mar  3 01:27:09.542: INFO: waiting for 3 replicas (current: 1)
Mar  3 01:27:29.543: INFO: waiting for 3 replicas (current: 1)
Mar  3 01:27:29.774: INFO: RC test-deployment: sending request to consume 0 MB
Mar  3 01:27:29.774: INFO: ConsumeMem URL: {https   172.19.116.45:443 /api/v1/namespaces/horizontal-pod-autoscaling-470/services/test-deployment-ctrl/proxy/ConsumeMem  false durationSec=30&megabytes=0&requestSizeMegabytes=100 }
Mar  3 01:27:30.052: INFO: RC test-deployment: sending request to consume 0 of custom metric QPS
Mar  3 01:27:30.052: INFO: ConsumeCustomMetric URL: {https   172.19.116.45:443 /api/v1/namespaces/horizontal-pod-autoscaling-470/services/test-deployment-ctrl/proxy/BumpMetric  false delta=0&durationSec=30&metric=QPS&requestSizeMetrics=10 }
```
By idea such requests goes through controller and then - controller sending it to consumers. But consumers continue consume 1Mi MEM and 0 CPU even in case I saw a request from e2e to controller.
```
freerunner@pegassie:[~/metrics-server] (master)$ kubectl top pod -n horizontal-pod-autoscaling-470
NAME                               CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
test-deployment-5948f49fb8-c97p7   0m           1Mi
```

Metrics-server works fine because logging in to container and execute some primitive operations did its job and normal metrics was caught. 

Then I tried to execute curl command manually to make consume request.
`curl --data "millicores=300&durationSec=600" http://10.233.97.21:8080/ConsumeCPU`
And it worked as expected. (HPA also)
```
root@kaas-node-b3de5b83-1f27-439d-85d5-909a86509de0:~# kubectl top po -n horizontal-pod-autoscaling-470
NAME                               CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
test-deployment-5948f49fb8-c97p7   300m         6Mi
test-deployment-5948f49fb8-hgrbj   0m           1Mi
```

Then, in tries to find root cause I found that:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/images/agnhost/resource-consumer-controller/controller.go#L216

So, controller construct an URL to reach consumers that for sure will not work with domains that not 'cluster.local`.
Moreover - controller does not write any logs that may help to debug issues with that.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.16.7/v1.17.3/v1.18.0-beta/master
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Openstack VMs
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): 
NAME="Ubuntu"
VERSION="18.04.2 LTS (Bionic Beaver)"
ID=ubuntu
ID_LIKE=debian
PRETTY_NAME="Ubuntu 18.04.2 LTS"
VERSION_ID="18.04"
HOME_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/"
SUPPORT_URL="https://help.ubuntu.com/"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/"
PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="https://www.ubuntu.com/legal/terms-and-policies/privacy-policy"
VERSION_CODENAME=bionic
UBUNTU_CODENAME=bionic
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux kaas-node-b3de5b83-1f27-439d-85d5-909a86509de0 4.15.0-51-generic #55-Ubuntu SMP Wed May 15 14:27:21 UTC 2019 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Install tools: Kubespray

review_comments:
Can we please get a comment explaining how this is operating and why?  It's PROBABLY safe, all things considered, but it's a heuristic.

This has come up in other places, and we really ought to expose it through downward API or something like that.

Maybe it is good to have comments, but even this module has more complex functions without comments.
According to the activity on the bug-report which gets fixed here, no one really cared about it. So, I wonder exactly where it has come up?

Past mistakes do not mean we shouldn't do better.  The function is sufficiently subtle that having an explanation of what it is supposed to be doing and why is justified.  I'm not asking for a book, just a couple sentences. Less than this comment, probably.
Added comment in the code here and in the place of it's call.

are other tests depending on this?
should not keep it as default?
With proposed change we will have working DNS suffix, because it is taken from real DNS config. So, if "cluster.local" is configured, it will be picked up. That's the trick.
is there a reason not to use `http://%s.%s.svc:%d%s`? that also resolves to the service and doesn't require custom DNS suffix lookup

> is there a reason not to use `http://%s.%s.svc:%d%s`? that also resolves to the service and doesn't require custom DNS suffix lookup

I was not sure whether it is needed for someone to use full DNS name or not. So, kept the behaviour - full DNS name having correct suffix. For HPA tests just "svc" is enough.
I don't mind to simplify the PR to just removing this ".cluster.local" part of DNS. Should I?
No, leave it as full DNS name, otherwise it'll break Windows. :) It doesn't like partially qualified names, and that would break some tests.
so... windows doesn't support the kube approach to dns?

That is a bit vague, tbh. But if you are referring to supporting PQDNs, then no. It's been known for quite a while that Windows doesn't support PQDNs (basically, any DNS name that contains a dot will be treated as a FQDN. Shortnames are fine though. For example, in the default namespace, ``kubernetes`` is resolvable.)

https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/3521

Also, some of the tests that using / testing PQDNs have been tagged as ``[LinuxOnly]`` too: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75758
So, if it is a must to keep old behavior then, I guess, we keep it as is and can move on.
WRT Windows, this is one of a long list of things that don't work right in Windows which were deemed "acceptable because no Windows user would expect them to work", even if a Kube user would.  Sigh.
FWIW using strings.Fields() would be safer WRT repeated whitespace
The only thing that is changed here is that function becomes exported having uppercase first letter. So, I do not understand the point of the comment.
exporting it and starting to use it as a utility method for other packages expands the scope of the code and increases the importance that it be robust/correct

Strictly speaking this function gets a list of "search paths" and if I were to find "" in that list (which you would if there was a double-space) I would be very surprised.

Is there a test-case for this function?  I'm not going to demand you go write one, unless you want to, but it probably should have a test including values with duplicate whitespace

@liggitt , @thockin I agree that it would be good to fix this thing, but I disagree that it must be part of this particular change that has one concrete goal - fixing concrete bug. And the change you propose me doing is not related to the bugfix at all.

Then, about unit tests, the fact that I changed the name of the function and unit tests passed means that there are either no tests or they were not run. In anyway, it doesn't get tested on regular basis. So, it has much more TODOs which must be done, but definitely not as part of this change, IMHO.
